import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1101

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1101](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1101)
-/

open Nat Filter

namespace Erdos1101

/-- The set of integers not divisible by any u_i. -/
def ASet (u : ℕ → ℕ) : Set ℕ :=
  { a | ∀ i, ¬ u i ∣ a }

/-- The sequence of integers A_u which are not divisible by any u_i
arranged in a monotonic sequence. -/
noncomputable def A (u : ℕ → ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.nth (fun a => a ∈ ASet u) n

/-- t_x such that u_0 ... u_{t_x-1} ≤ x < u_0 ... u_{t_x}.
-/
noncomputable def t (u : ℕ → ℕ) (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup { k | ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, u i ≤ x }

/-- A sequence is "good" if
1. it is strictly monotone
2. it is pairwise coprime
3. the sum of reciprocals converges
4. the gap between consecutive elements in A(u) is bounded relative to t_x. -/
def IsGood (u : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  StrictMono u ∧
  (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Coprime (u i) (u j)) ∧
  Summable (fun n => 1 / (u n : ℝ)) ∧
  ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
    ∀ k, A u k < x →
      (A u (k + 1) : ℝ) - A u k < (1 + ε) * (t u x : ℝ) * (∏' i : ℕ, (1 - 1 / (u i : ℝ)))⁻¹

/-- 1. There is NO good sequence with polynomial growth. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1101.parts.i :
    ¬ ∃ u, IsGood u ∧ ∃ k : ℕ, (fun n => (u n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ k) := by
  sorry

/-- 2. There is a good sequence with sub-exponential growth. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1101.parts.ii :
    ∃ u, IsGood u ∧ (fun n => Real.log (u n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1101

status_issues.source_status: The source discussion records a positive resolution of the second question by Peter Li, announced April 27, 2026. His paper's Theorem 1 constructs a good sequence of primes with log(u_n) = sqrt(n) + O(n^(-1/2)), which implies the precise subexponential assertion in this declaration. Nat Sothanaphan reported a check on April 28. The overall problem page still says OPEN; this update concerns only part (ii).
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/1101#post-5956 links Li's A Subexponential Good Sequence. At https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/1101#post-5985, Nat Sothanaphan writes: “Congrats. Standard check found no issues” and identifies the result as “the positive resolution to the second question.” The linked paper, dated April 27, 2026, states the construction in Theorem 1.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change only Erdos1101.erdos_1101.parts.ii to category research solved and cite Li's paper and the source announcement. Retain the theorem's positive assertion; part (i) can remain research open.

reformulations.difference: The source bounds a maximum of consecutive gaps and multiplies reciprocal Euler factors. Lean bounds every eligible gap and takes the reciprocal of the infinite product.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under IsGood, every u i is at least 2, ASet u is infinite, and A is strictly increasing. Thus only finitely many indices satisfy A u k < x, and this set is nonempty for x > 1; bounding its maximum is equivalent to bounding every member. Summability of the reciprocals implies that the product of 1 - 1/u i converges to a positive real number, so its inverse equals the product of the inverse factors. The finite-maximum equivalence and product identity are proved in scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean quantifies the sufficiently large cutoff x over natural numbers; the source's cutoff can also be read as real-valued.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The real-cutoff condition immediately implies the natural-cutoff condition. Conversely, use n = ceil(x). Every integer A u k < x is also < n. Since the prefix products are strictly increasing integers, t(n) is at most t(x) + 1. Moreover t(x) tends to infinity. Apply the natural-cutoff condition with ε/2; eventually (1 + ε/2)(t(x) + 1) ≤ (1 + ε)t(x). This recovers the real-cutoff condition, so discretization does not change goodness.

reformulations.difference: Polynomial growth is expressed as existence of a natural exponent k with u = O(n^k), rather than the source's u_n < n^{O(1)}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An eventual bound u_n ≤ C n^k implies u_n < n^(k+1) once n > max(C,1). Conversely, an eventual strict power bound implies the corresponding Big-O bound. Allowing only integer exponents loses nothing, since any fixed real exponent can be enlarged to an integer. The Big-O/eventual strict integer-power equivalence is proved in scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Subexponential growth is expressed as log(u_n) = o(n), rather than u_n ≤ exp(o(n)); the original paper expresses it as u_n^(1/n) → 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: IsGood forces u_n ≥ 2, so the logarithms are defined in their ordinary positive-input sense and are nonnegative. Taking logarithms shows equivalence to: for every ε > 0, eventually u_n ≤ exp(ε n). This equivalence is proved in scratch.lean. Equivalently log(u_n)/n tends to zero, and exponentiating gives the original nth-root limit.

review.notes: All six declarations were checked against the cited statement and the relevant original-paper passage. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles cleanly. It proves that IsGood excludes 0 and 1, that ASet is infinite under the admissibility hypotheses, that Nat.nth therefore enumerates it correctly, and that t satisfies the intended prefix-product inequalities for x ≥ 1. It also contains concrete small-value tests and the stated growth/product/maximum checks. The tested lemmas have no sorryAx dependency. No answer(...) or formal_proof records occur in this file. The reviewed file was not modified.
